full_text: Consider the following schema of a database used in a vehicle rental system. Customers (custld: integer, name: varchar (50), address: varachar (60), phone: char (10)) Vehicles (vehicleld: interger, mileage: double, fuel Type: varchar (10), transmission: varchar (15)) Reservations (cld: integer, vId: integer, startDate: datetime, endDate: datetime, returnDate: datetime) Payments (pld: integer, cId: integer, vId: integer, type: varchar (10), amount: real, date: datetime) Customers table contains attributes to store the id (custld), name, address and the phone number of customers. Vehicles table contains the id (vehicleld), milage, type of fuel and the type of transmission (transmission) for each vehicle. Fuel type attribute stores Petrol, Diesel or Hybrid. The transmission attribute stores either automatic or manual. Reservation table stores information about reservations of vehicles. The table contains information about the vehicles which have been rented (vId), the customers who have reserved vehicles (cId), start dates of the reservations (startDate), the end dates of the reservations (endDate) and the dates the vehicles have been returned by the customer (returnDate). For vehicles that are not returned yet, a null value is stored in the return date field. Payment table stores the payment details of the reservations. The table contains payment id (pId), customer id (cId), vehicle id (vId), type of the payment (type), amount paid and the and the paid date. When customers reserve vehicles they have to make the full payment or a partial payment. If the vehicle is returned late a fine has to be paid for the vehicle. The type attribute of the payment table stores Full, Partial or Fine to show the type of the payment as above. The primary keys of all relations are underlined.

The 'Room' table tracks details about the hotel's rooms. It includes information such as the room number, room type, bed type, price per night, and a flag (boolean) indicating whether the room is currently occupied. The 'Booking' table manages guest reservations. Each booking is assigned a unique ID and is associated with a specific guest (via guestId) and a room (via roomNum). It also records the check-in and check-out dates, as well as the total booking amount. The 'Bill' table handles billing information for guest stays. It connects to a particular booking (via bookingId) and stores the bill number, the total amount to be paid, the payment method, and the payment status. The 'Receptionist' table contains details about hotel receptionist, with each staff member having a unique ID, name, phone number, and address. This allows the system to keep track of receptionists or other staff members involved in hotel operations.

Qualifications table stores information related to the qualifications of lecturers. The table stores the IDs of the lecturers (lecturerld) and the qualifications they have received (such as BSc in IT , MSc in GIS , MBA and Phd in Computer Science ). The Teach table stores information on teaching. For those who play instruments, their specialization, and the duration that they play should be stored. For each instrument, a unique identification number and the name (e.g., guitar, violin, flute, etc.) are recorded. Each student capable of playing instruments may play several instruments, and a given instrument is played by one student. A student who plays instruments may supervise several other such students. Each album has a unique identification number, title, copyright date and a format (e.g., CD or MC). Each album has one student who acts as its producer. A student may produce several albums. Each album has several songs on it and a song appears on one album. The date that the songs are recorded on the album should be known. For each song a unique identification number, the title and the author are recorded. Each song is sung by one or more students, and a student sings several songs. The number of times that a song is sung should be recorded. Each song may have several melody types. For each melody type, the tempo, and the key for that song (e.g. C major, D minor etc.) are recorded. Different songs may have the same key.

full_text: Consider a relation R (A, B, C, D, E, F, G) with the following set of functional dependencies over R: F = {A->BC, B->D, C->EF, AC->G}

subquestions.label: a)
subquestions.text: Find all the keys in relation R using attribute closure method.

subquestions.label: b)
subquestions.text: Is R in 3NF? Give reasons for your conclusion.

subquestions.label: c)
subquestions.text: Is R in BCNF? Give reasons for your conclusion. If R is not in BCNF, convert it to a set of BCNF relations.
